Resolve horizontally first: notice that $P$ has no horizontal component! This gives a single equation in $\theta$: $10\cos 25^\circ = 2\cos 40^\circ + 16\sin\theta$.
walkthrough: Let us inspect each of the four coplanar forces acting at the point from the diagram:
1. Force $P\text{ N}$ acts directly vertically upwards along the positive $y$-axis. Its horizontal component is $0$ and its vertical component is $+P$.
2. Force $10\text{ N}$ acts in the fourth quadrant at an angle of $25^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis. Its components are $+10\cos 25^\circ$ horizontally and $-10\sin 25^\circ$ vertically.
3. Force $2\text{ N}$ acts in the third quadrant at an angle of $40^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis. Its components are $-2\cos 40^\circ$ horizontally and $-2\sin 40^\circ$ vertically.
4. Force $16\text{ N}$ acts in the third quadrant at an angle $\theta$ to the negative $y$-axis. Its components are $-16\sin\theta$ horizontally and $-16\cos\theta$ vertically.
Because the system is in static equilibrium, the resultant force in every direction must be zero.

Step 1: Resolve forces horizontally. Since $P$ is purely vertical, resolving horizontally isolates $\theta$ into a single equation:
$$\sum F_x = 10\cos 25^\circ - 2\cos 40^\circ - 16\sin\theta = 0$$

Step 2: Resolve forces vertically to find the magnitude of $P$:
$$\sum F_y = P - 10\sin 25^\circ - 2\sin 40^\circ - 16\cos\theta = 0$$
$$P = 10\sin 25^\circ + 2\sin 40^\circ + 16\cos(28.077^\circ)$$
Thus, the angle is $\theta = 28.1^\circ$ and the force magnitude is $P = 19.6\text{ N}$.
